findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() — unwrap on I/O result panics on file-not-found, permissions, or encoding errors
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed ParseError/IOError
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use map_err on fs::read_to_string

findings.problem: load_packets returns Vec<Record> with no MAX_DOMAIN_* cap on line count; every line allocates a Vec<String>
findings.failure_mode: hostile input (millions of lines) causes unbounded heap growth and OOM
findings.fix: accept a MAX_LINES domain cap, return Result, cap allocations, and reject excess lines with a typed Error variant

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — unwrap on parse panics on non-numeric input
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line aborts the entire batch instead of returning a typed parse error for that record
findings.fix: map_err(parse_err) to a RecordParseError variant and either skip with a warning or fail the entire batch with typed error

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] — unchecked indexing into Vec with no bounds check
findings.failure_mode: line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields causes panic via index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: use parts.first() and parts.get(1) and return a typed error for malformed lines

findings.problem: .parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 — lossy as cast from u32 to u16 silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: a value like 70000 parses as u32 fine then wraps to 4464, silently corrupting domain data with no error
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| RecordError::ValueOutOfRange) to reject values outside u16 range

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — hidden I/O side effect fused inside the parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: side effect in pure-looking core logic makes the function non-deterministic, non-testable, and couples data loading to stdout
findings.fix: move all I/O to the shell boundary; return parsed data from the core and handle logging in the action layer

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path) — hidden I/O in a function that reads a file path string parameter
findings.failure_mode: the function signature `load_packets(path: &str) -> Vec<Record>` hides the fact that it performs file system I/O, making it indistinguishable from pure data loading
findings.fix: rename to reflect I/O (e.g., `load_packets_from_file`) or split: pure parser takes &str content, shell layer handles fs::read_to_string

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 with public fields — no smart constructor, no newtype for value, no validation
findings.failure_mode: any code can construct Record { name: String::new(), value: 0 } or Record { name: "".to_string(), value: 65535 } with no domain enforcement
findings.fix: make fields private, add a smart constructor `Record::new(name: &str, value: u16) -> Result<Record, RecordError>` with validation, and use newtype for value if domain rules apply

findings.problem: load_packets returns Vec<Record> — no error type at all; all failures are panics via unwrap
findings.failure_mode: caller has no way to distinguish file-not-found, parse errors, index errors, or overflow — all manifest as panic
findings.fix: return `Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>` with variants like FileNotFound, Parse(RecordParseError), Overflow for typed railway-oriented error handling

findings.problem: part.trim().to_string() creates intermediate owned String per field when &str would suffice for the core logic
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary heap allocations per field in the hot path of parsing; scales poorly with input size
findings.fix: parse from &str directly and only allocate the final String for the Record name; avoid collecting trimmed copies into Vec<String>

residual_risk: Static review only — no commands run, no tests executed, no proofs or benchmarks performed. The crate contains multiple blocker-class violations (unwrap on I/O, unwrap on parse, unchecked indexing, lossy cast, unbounded allocation, hidden I/O in core, no typed errors) that would likely cause panics or data corruption under hostile input. All unwrap calls must be replaced with typed error propagation, unchecked indexing must use get/first, the u32-to-u16 cast must use try_from, the println must be removed from core logic, and a domain cap with Result return type must be added.
